key_insight: HiVLA separates high-level semantic reasoning (a VLM planner) from low-level motor control via explicit visual grounding, preserving VLM reasoning while enabling robust, specialized control.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off where fine-tuning end-to-end Vision-Language-Action models for control degrades their VLM-inherited reasoning and generalization, making it hard to get both strong semantic planning and reliable motor execution.
method: Hierarchical design: a VLM-based high-level planner generates task steps and goals in semantic, scene-aware language.
Visual-grounding module: maps planner outputs to scene-centric signals (object masks, keypoints, affordance maps) to localize goals in the current view.
Modular low-level controller: a dedicated motion/controller module consumes grounded signals to execute actions; modules are trained or fine-tuned separately to preserve VLM reasoning.
impact: Enables modular, sample-efficient embodied manipulation that retains advanced VLM reasoning while achieving reliable motor performance—useful for building interpretable, generalizable robotic systems and reducing catastrophic fine-tuning effects.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: VLM planner → visual grounding → low-level controller (with arrows showing information flow).
Task storyboard: sequential frames showing a complex manipulation task decomposed into high-level steps and grounded targets.
Comparison chart: performance and reasoning retention vs. end-to-end VLA fine-tuning (e.g., success rate, reasoning score).
Grounding overlays: example camera views with object masks/keypoints/affordance heatmaps produced by the grounding module.
paper_title: HiVLA: A Visual-Grounded-Centric Hierarchical Embodied Manipulation System
paper_authors: Tianshuo Yang, Guanyu Chen, Yutian Chen, Zhixuan Liang, Yitian Liu
